title: The char-p energy SURPLUS E_p-E_inf is a Stepanov point-count, not a Weil/moment one
evidence: Exact integer probes (proper dyadic subgroups mu_n, n=8/16/32, proper-subgroup primes p=1 mod n, n^2<<p, beta in [3,5]) in scripts/probes/_407_conn/probe_C029_surplus_stepanov.py, probe_C029_floorcross.py, probe_C029_norm_mechanism.py. THREE findings. (1) ISOLATION IS REAL (matches the 3 in-tree bricks): surplus S_r := E_r^{F_p} - E_r^inf is non-negative in every instance, and the char-0 part E_r^inf is exactly governed (E_r^inf computed by antipodal signed-multiset reduction zeta^{a+n/2}=-zeta^a; matches repCount_le_two/bessel_energy_le_gaussian). (2) THE 'STEPANOV CEILING' IS THE TRIVIAL EQUIDISTRIBUTION HEURISTIC, NOT A STEPANOV BOUND: S_r <= ~0.6*n^{2r}/p in every case (never explodes, Q1 of the attack_plan confirmed) -- but n^{2r}/p is exactly |image of the mod-p sum map|^{-1}*n^{2r}, the random/equidistribution count; in probe_C029_floorcross part (A), growing p at fixed (n=16,r=4) the surplus does NOT track c*n^{2r}/p, it COLLAPSES to 0 once p exceeds the box (p=4129->183680, p=20593->0). So 'Stepanov point-count' is a RELABELING of the equidistribution ceiling; Stepanov supplies nothing the trivial fiber count does not. (3) THE SUB-FLOOR CLAIM FAILS IN THE OPERATIVE BAND AND THE MECHANISM IS THE NORM-DIVISIBILITY WALL: surplus is sub-floor (S_r << n^r) only when p>>n^r i.e. r<beta; at r>=beta the data gives surp/floor = 2.80 (n=16,r=4,beta=3) and 16.18 (n=32,r=4,beta=3). The prize OPERATIVE moment is r~ln q >> beta (deep-moment optimum, memory O389), exactly where the surplus dominates the floor by n^{2r-beta}. probe_C029_norm_mechanism shows a surplus tuple <=> a nonzero short signed root-sum alpha (<=2r roots) with p | N(alpha); the largest proper-subgroup prime carrying a surplus grows toward the house (2r)^{n/2} (n=16: max_p = 337/3361/10993 for r=2/3/4). At the prize (n=2^30, p~n^5) the house (2r)^{2^29} >> p, so the norm bound is VACUOUS (a short alpha CAN have a large prime factor p) -- the documented Cheng-house / large-sieve wall (memory arklib-407-largesieve-avgq-refuted).
honest_note: The three cited bricks (repCount_le_two -> E_inf<=3n^2; bessel_energy_le_gaussian -> E_r^inf<=(2r-1)!!n^r; the surplus decomposition) are GENUINELY PROVEN in-tree and the isolation of the surplus as the only open quantity is a real, correct, elegant result -- that part is PARTIAL-proven and uncontested. What I refute is the reclassification that buys the prize: the surplus is NOT a clean variety point-count that Stepanov bounds below the floor in the operative regime. Its only available ceiling n^{2r}/p is the trivial equidistribution count (no Stepanov needed) and it is ABOVE the floor for r>=beta, which is precisely the prize's deep-moment band r~ln q. The surplus = #{short signed root-sums alpha != 0 with p|N(alpha)} is exactly the norm-divisibility object the campaign already studied (DISPROOF_LOG O134/O135/O141/O143; O135 measured +33.6% surplus at r=5 -- consistent with my surp/floor>1 at large r), which welds to BGK/Cheng-house. I did not run Lean (no new lemma to land; the cited lemmas are already in-tree). Probes are exact integer arithmetic at proper subgroups/large primes, the prescribed non-degenerate regime; small-n extrapolation to n=2^30 is by the house/norm scaling argument, not measured at prize scale. NO closure; not a refutation of any lemma so no DISPROOF_LOG entry needed, but the 'surplus crosses floor at r=beta' boundary and 'ceiling = equidistribution not Stepanov' are new sharpenings.
wall: W-BGK: equivalently the norm-divisibility / Cheng-house large-sieve wall. The surplus is exactly #{short signed root-sums alpha=sum x - sum y on mu_n^{2r}, alpha != 0, with p | N(alpha)}; bounding it below the floor for the operative r~ln q is the same square-root-cancellation-for-thin-mu_n core (the surplus IS the char-p cancellation defect, not a separable clean point-count). Stepanov's auxiliary-degree wall is the same wall under a different name (cf. in-tree repCount_two_mul_le_of_pow_ne_one giving only r(c)<=(n+1)/2, the order-2 base case; pushing vanishing order to ~n^{1/3} is the open construction).
